Zocdoc integrates with doctors’ scheduling systems using a mix of direct API connections, middleware partnerships, calendar syncing, and manual/partial integrations. * Native API integrations: Zocdoc connects directly to the PMS or EHR vendor’s scheduling API when the vendor exposes robust endpoints (appointments CRUD, availability queries, cancellations, rescheduling, patient info). * Middleware / integration platforms: When direct APIs aren’t available or consistent, Zocdoc uses intermediaries (integration platforms or health-data middleware) that normalize multiple PMS/EHR protocols into a standard interface Zocdoc consumes. * Calendar/ICS sync and single-sign-on adapters: For smaller practices or systems without open APIs, Zocdoc can sync via secure calendar protocols (iCal/ICS) or use connectors that read/write provider calendars (Office 365, Google Calendar) or use SSO-enabled vendor adapters. * Manual and hybrid workflows: Practices that cannot support automated sync use a hybrid model: Zocdoc shows availability based on a schedule set in its portal and forwards bookings to staff as confirmation requests. * Small practice setups: Often use Google/Office calendars or proprietary scheduling; Zocdoc uses calendar sync or practice-managed availability in those cases. Zocdoc integrates through a spectrum: direct API/FHIR for full two‑way, near‑real‑time scheduling; middleware and calendar connectors for mixed capability vendors; and manual/hybrid workflows where automation isn’t possible.
